Mr. Huai Zhun is living in the suburbs with the style of Pei Zhenzi, and Beihong painted a chicken to congratulate him, which was inscribed by Dafu in the autumn of Jimao. Inscribed underneath are "Tuzhong Trailing Tail Sheng", a rectangular seal in vermilion, and "Yu Dafu", a square seal in white.　　Twenty-eight years refers to the twenty-eighth year of the Republic of China (1939), when Xu Beihong was 44 years old.　　After the "July 7th" Incident at Lugou Bridge in 1937, Xu Beihong went to Hong Kong, Singapore, Kuala Lumpur, Penang and other places to hold relief exhibitions with a sense of national tragedy. During his stay in Singapore, he met and became close friends with Mr. Han Huaijun. This picture is a small painting painted by Xu Beihong to congratulate Mr. Han Huaijun on his housewarming, and asked Yu Dafu, who lived there, to inscribe it, showing their deep friendship.　　The picture depicts a cockerel standing in front of a lush bamboo forest with its head held high, looking peaceful and self-possessed. The chicken is sketched in a few strokes, with an accurate structure, fluffy and soft feathers, and vivid brushwork, showing the author's keen observation and strong modeling skills.　　The author wishes his friends good fortune by painting chickens with the auspicious sound of "ji". At the same time, the chicken has the reputation of "five virtues", and people believe that it is based on its appearance and habits: the Chinese, with a Chinese crown on its head; the martial, with claws that can fight; the brave, with the courage to fight in front of the enemy; the benevolent, to greet its kind when it sees food; and the letter, to report the dawn without fail. The author uses the painting of the chicken to praise the beauty of its friends who possess the five virtues of literature, martial arts, courage, benevolence and faith.
